newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance bids for airport project.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance bids for airport project.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries Ltd is among four consortiums bidding for a multi-million dollar new airport project near Bombay, a state-run firm said on Tuesday.

City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) said Reliance Industries was the lead partner in a consortium for a $490 million new domestic airport at New Bombay, a new township just off Bombay.
The consortium included Carter & Burgess, Pacific Alliance Capital Group and Hellmuth Obata Kassabham Inc, all of the U.S., CIDCO said in a statement.

Ispat Industries Ltd headed another consortium, which included Parsons Inc, U.S.A, and India Development Finance Ltd, that have have submitted prequalification bids, CIDCO managing director Vishwas Dhumal told reporters.
Germany-based Rishi Value Marketing was the lead partner of another consortium. Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG, Lufthansa Consulting GmbH and Messe Munchen GmbH were members of this group, he said.

Boss Technologies Ltd, based in Bombay, led the fourth consortium with Sir William Halcrow & Partners, Taylor Woodrow Consortium Ltd, a unit of Taylor Woodrow Plc and SERCO-IAL Systems Ltd of SERCO Group Plc, all of the U.K., CIDCO said.
The bidders have to simultaneously take up a $86 million international exhibition centre, adjacent to the new airport, Dhumal said.
The consortiums now have to submit detailed technical and financial bids, he added added.
